Include a dramatic icy slope as the focal play field, a rider in motion, a clearly readable route, gates and obstacles ahead, speed and distance HUD, directional controls, and a compact progress indicator. Put strong emphasis on the sensation of speed, immediate obstacle readability, a distinct alpine identity, clear hierarchy, and polished visual finish.

Clarity & Hierarchy: the HUD clusters are legible but compete — the centered 'DESCENT 3%' bar overlaps the mountain strip and hangs awkwardly under the 'LIVE DESCENT' pill, creating two rival top status zones against the top-right score panel, while the empty middle gives the eye no focal anchor and the faint lower-right lines read as a placeholder rather than a route. Visual System & Craft: components are clean (rounded glass panels, consistent type) but a hard horizontal seam at ~28% splits the sky/mountains from the void like a layout bug instead of a horizon, the palette is near-monochrome with only the orange logo/speed bar and yellow flag as accents, and there is no depth, perspective, ice texture, or snow spray, so the claimed 'polished finish' is undercut by the unfinished field. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness: the alpine identity is thin — a row of generic flat triangles plus a logo — with no parallax, fog, light, or particle atmosphere, so it reads as a generic dashboard rather than a fast alpine descent. Core trade-off: the HUD is over-built relative to the missing play field, and the motion cues (streaks/blur) needed to sell speed will collide with the need for crisp, instantly readable gates.
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan, all CSS/SVG/canvas, no external assets. (1) Build the focal slope first: fill the lower ~70% with a perspective ice surface (trapezoid converging to a vanishing point at the horizon), a curving route ribbon with moving lane dashes, and ice texture via repeating-linear-gradient; replace the hard 28% seam with a real horizon using an atmospheric fog gradient so the mountains sit behind the slope. (2) Place the rider in motion as an SVG silhouette centered on the route with a lean/tilt, contact shadow, and snow-spray particles, animated with a subtle bob and steer-tilt. (3) Add gates and obstacles along the ribbon with perspective scaling (farther = higher/smaller), using high-contrast silhouettes — warm-orange slalom gates against pale ice — for immediate readability. (4) Sell speed in the periphery only: parallax on the mountain strip, FOV/zoom tied to the 205 km/h, and streaks at the screen edges, keeping the gate zone crisp so motion never hurts obstacle legibility. (5) Re-tune hierarchy: demote the top 'DESCENT' bar to a slim top-edge strip so the top-right score panel and bottom-left speed panel become the two clear anchors and the rider becomes the center of gravity. (6) Deepen alpine identity with a layered parallax mountain range, a cool key light, horizon fog, and drifting snow particles. (7) Unify the system: reserve one warm accent for gates/boost, use ice-blue for everything else, add a subtle vignette, and verify no HUD clipping on the new field.
